material_findings: V6 is now the live paper champion and its external bridge is wired to telemetry, but current external telemetry has zero accepted Kalshi matches despite scanning 2500 Kalshi markets.

The incumbent Kalshi score_pair uses lexical overlap, sequence similarity, numeric compatibility, orientation and expiry but never applies detect_asset/classify_market as a hard entity-compatibility gate.

Current mapping diagnostics therefore rank cross-asset pairs such as Polymarket Bitcoin thresholds against Kalshi silver/gold thresholds. These are rejected by weak aggregate score today, but lowering the match threshold without an entity gate would convert a data-quality defect into false external probabilities.
A research-aggressive matcher should first hard-require entity/asset compatibility and only then broaden the universe and lower soft score/margin/confidence floors.

top_near_candidate.note: This is a short-horizon feature backtest, not an approved terminal probability, so it must not be fabricated into q_external.

required_next_evidence: Run incumbent and entity-aware aggressive matcher on the same point-in-time Polymarket/Kalshi universe and report accepted/rejected pairs by reason.
Require manual or rule-derived proposition equivalence on a sample of newly admitted cross-venue matches before interpreting Kalshi price as a terminal probability.
For direct probabilities, evaluate terminal Brier/log-loss and calibration by time-to-resolution against contemporaneous Polymarket probability, then executable paper PnL at 1x, 1.5x and 2x costs.
Do not route the Binance realized-vol near-candidate through the terminal-probability external bridge; it needs a separate short-horizon external-RV model if pursued.
